section.heading: Authorisations in an emergency—imminent risk to safety of an Australian person

content.p: When this section applies
This section applies if an agency head is satisfied that:
there is, or is likely to be, an imminent risk to the safety of an Australian person who is outside Australia; and

it is necessary or desirable to undertake an activity, or a series of activities, for the specific purpose, or for purposes which include the specific purpose, of producing intelligence on the person; and
it is not reasonably practicable to obtain the person’s consent to the agency producing that intelligence; and
having regard to the nature and gravity of the risk, it is reasonable to believe that the person would consent to the agency producing that intelligence if the person were able to do so.
Authorisation
The agency head may, orally or in writing, give an authorisation under this section for the activity, or series of activities, if the agency head is satisfied that, apart from paragraph 9(1A)(b):
the facts of the case would justify the responsible Minister giving an authorisation under section 9 because the agency head is satisfied that the conditions in subsections 9(1) and (1A) are met; and
the responsible Minister would have given the authorisation.
Conditions on authorisation
The authorisation is subject to any conditions specified by the agency head.
Agency head to record and notify

As soon as practicable after giving the authorisation (but no later than 8 hours after the authorisation is given) the agency head must, orally or in writing, notify the responsible Minister of the authorisation.
As soon as practicable after giving the authorisation (but no later than 48 hours after the authorisation is given) the agency head must:
if the authorisation is given orally—ensure that the authorisation is recorded in writing; and
ensure that a summary of the facts of the case that the agency head was satisfied justified giving the authorisation is recorded in writing; and
give to the responsible Minister:
a copy of the authorisation; and
a summary of the facts of the case that the agency head was satisfied justified giving the authorisation; and
an explanation of the Minister’s obligation under subsection (6); and
give to the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security the documents referred to in subparagraphs (c)(i) and (ii); and

(e) if the Australian person is, or is likely to be, involved in an activity or activities that are, or are likely to be, a threat to security—give to the Attorney-General and the Minister responsible for administering the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979 (the ASIO Minister) the documents referred to in subparagraphs (c)(i) and (ii).
Role of responsible Minister
The responsible Minister must, as soon as practicable after being given documents under paragraph (5)(c), consider whether to cancel the authorisation under subsection (10).

If the Attorney-General is required to be given documents under paragraph (5)(e), the responsible Minister must have regard to any advice given by the Attorney-General when making a decision under subsection (6).
Role of Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security
Within 30 days after the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security is given documents under paragraph (5)(d), the Inspector-General must:
consider whether the agency head has complied with the requirements of this section; and
provide the responsible Minister with a report on the Inspector-General’s views of the extent of the compliance by the agency head with the requirements of this section; and
provide to the Committee a copy of the conclusions in the report.
Period of effect of authorisation
The authorisation ceases to have effect at the earliest of the following times:
the end of 6 months, starting on the day the authorisation is given;
if the authorisation specifies a time when the authorisation ceases to have effect—that time;
if the responsible Minister cancels the authorisation under subsection (10)—the time of cancellation;
if the agency head cancels the authorisation under subsection (12)—the time of cancellation;
if an authorisation for the activity, or series of activities, is given under section 9, 9A or 9B—the time the authorisation under section 9, 9A or 9B is given.
Cancellation by responsible Minister
The responsible Minister may, in writing, cancel the authorisation.
If the responsible Minister cancels the authorisation under subsection (10), the Minister must, as soon as practicable, give written notice of the cancellation to:
the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security; and
if the Attorney-General and the ASIO Minister are required to be given documents under paragraph (5)(e)—those Ministers.
Cancellation by agency head
The agency head must, in writing, cancel the authorisation if the agency head is satisfied that:
there is not; and
there is not likely to be;
a significant risk to the safety of the Australian person.
Note: The agency head may cancel the authorisation in other circumstances (see subsection 33(3) of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901).
If the agency head cancels the authorisation under subsection (12), the agency head must, as soon as practicable, give written notice of the cancellation to:
the responsible Minister; and
the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security; and
if the Attorney-General and the ASIO Minister are required to be given documents under paragraph (5)(e)—those Ministers.
Delegation
An agency head may, in writing, delegate to a staff member (other than a consultant or contractor) all or any of the powers, functions or duties of the agency head under this section.
Note: See sections 34AA, 34AB and 34A of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 on delegations.
In exercising a power, performing a function or discharging a duty under a delegation under subsection (14), the delegate must comply with any written directions of the agency head.
Relationship with the Acts Interpretation Act 1901
(16) To avoid doubt, this section does not limit subsection 33(3) of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 to the extent that it applies to an authorisation given under this section.
Status of instruments
The following are not legislative instruments:
an authorisation given in writing under subsection (2);
a written notice given under subsection (4), (11) or (13);
a record made, or a summary or explanation given, under subsection (5);
a report under subsection (8);
a cancellation under subsection (10) or (12).

section.heading: Rules to protect privacy of Australians—DIO

content.p: The responsible Minister in relation to DIO must make written rules regulating the communication and retention by DIO of intelligence information concerning Australian persons.
DIO must not communicate intelligence information concerning Australian persons, except in accordance with the rules.

In making the rules, the Minister must have regard to the need to ensure that the privacy of Australian persons is preserved as far as is consistent with the proper performance by DIO of its functions.
Before making the rules, the Minister must consult with:
the Attorney-General; and
the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security; and
the Director of DIO.

For the purpose of consultations under paragraphs (4)(a) and (b), the Minister must provide a copy of the rules the Minister is proposing to make to the Attorney-General and to the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security.

operationally sensitive information (within the meaning of Schedule 1); or

the performance by DIO of its functions.

approval for the person to exercise the authority was given before or after that commencement; or
the warrant to which the authority relates was issued before or after that commencement.
